references.observations: Owner's construction history: foundations in 1869, Gateway occupied in 1873, Palas topping-out in 1880, simplified Bower and Square Tower completed in 1892. Walls are brick with light limestone cladding. The unbuilt central keep and chapel are excluded.
references.planInterpretation: Inspected the 790 by 310 pixel labeled plan: Palas, two unequal spiral stairs, Bower, Knights' House, Square Tower, connecting range, gatehouse and two open courts. Manually transcribed part extents, approximately scaled at 0.194 m/pixel around pixel [395,155]. No scale bar or surveyed elevation was available; this is a proportional reconstruction inside the cached map precinct.

references.observations: Inspected the southern landscape panorama for overall limestone walls, dark roofs and mountain setting. The natural ridge is not included in this structural model.

South exterior: six Palas window ranks, paired arches, west open galleries, unequal stair towers, copper-colored dormers, steep slate roofs, corner bartizans and projecting Bower bays. Original photograph used for architectural observation; no pixels copied into textures.

Northwest aerial: northern Palas projection joins the main cylindrical stair, lower north range, Knights' House with corner turrets, and rectangular Square Tower with corbelled upper arcades, octagonal upper stage and pointed cap.

Outer gatehouse has brick wings, pale central portal with timber gate and sparse upper openings, stepped gable and cylindrical corner turrets. Exterior portal does not share the inner face's large triple windows. Heraldic relief and facade anchor ties remain pending.

Gatehouse court face is warm yellow/beige stone above a pale base, with a triple arcade/balcony and central clock in the stepped gable; end turrets have dark caps inside crenellated crowns. The photographed passage is open, while this current model depicts a closed timber gate; no interior passage is claimed.

Palas court gable has decorated lunettes, murals, suspended bartizans and central balcony. The north entrance stair rises along the gallery. Painted murals, exact sculpture and carved detail have not been reconstructed and keep maximum-fidelity review pending.

Cached exact Q4152 record is a castle precinct, historic=castle, with neither a building nor height tag. Its 159.33 by 66.264 m oriented envelope includes the open courts and is not an occupied footprint. Registration uses the signed frame, with separate occupied ranges derived from the official plan.

reconstruction.basis: Individual exterior reconstructed from the official labeled plan and inspected south, northwest, outer-gate and courtyard photographs. The cached OSM boundary is a precinct. Plan parts are manually transcribed and approximately scaled inside that boundary, not surveyed building footprints.
reconstruction.datum: Provisional lowest structural base, with raised retained courts. Real terrain/cliff contact is not established.

scaleBasis: OSM precinct establishes horizontal envelope and axis. Official plan establishes distinct parts. 65 m unreferenced cached height and photographic proportions are provisional vertical scale; no surveyed elevation drawing inspected.
limitations: Maximum exterior fidelity remains pending: plan transcription, floor heights, narrow roofs and tower profiles are photographic reconstructions, not measured elevations. The cached 65 m height has no cited source.
The unbuilt central keep and chapel are excluded. Current gatehouse and later Bower/Square Tower are represented; scaffolding and temporary conservation work are not architectural features.
Palas painted murals, heraldic portal relief, human/animal statues, carved capitals and exact tracery require dedicated sculptural/painting work. No substituted generic figure is claimed accurate.
No natural mountain, moat, forest or interiors are included. The retained court levels and basement walls require sloped-terrain integration; the model is a geographic draft.

All geometry is original. Reference images are linked, never embedded or copied into texture maps. Limestone, raw limestone, weathered limestone, sandstone, slate, copper, brick, painted metal and wood use canonical shared materials.

currentReview.scope: The detailed 20017068-byte234177-triangle original master remains independently reproducible at sha256:c78849de7780d2383656cb12873fabfc55a14e03a6ec92bc96be18d2d7ed3c8f from packages/worldgen/scripts/neuschwanstein-castle-model.mjs#neuschwansteinStudy.build. A separate reviewed model repairs individual occupied ranges against fresh attributable map polygons, including unequal stair towers, cranked Palas, open western galleries, dormers, Bower, Knights House, Square Tower, two open raised courts, connecting range and brick/ochre gatehouse with a genuinely open vaulted entry. Six common limestone, slate, painted metal, wood, copper and brick graphs use vertex tint; limestone is also a deliberately approximate common grain for carved/weathered and yellow gate stone, without claiming sandstone-specific bonds. Opaque glass/recess bring the near draw count to eight; no embedded images. Skyline uses baked common-graph linear means, district omits carved reveals and collapses fine paired openings, street/close retain framed arched windows and coarser circular roofs/crowns. Palas eave41.5/ridge54.5, stairs65/59.2, retained courts8.2/6.5 and gate33.9 remain provisional photographic working elevations, not measured sections. OSM height65 for north stair is independent map evidence, not a surveyed datum. Murals, sculpture, animals, heraldic relief and exact carving/tracery remain schematic or omitted; no visitor interiors, mountain mesh, forest, terrain, unbuilt keep/chapel or reference photograph textures. Gate vault, precinct edges and footprint approximations are not restoration-survey accuracy. Physical phone/laptop timings remain unmeasured. Automatic world placement remains disabled until the substantial relative terrain/court-level inconsistency is resolved.
currentReview.placement: Fresh exact-Q4152 castle precinct way221601969 contains individual Palas, Bower, Knights House, Square Tower, gatehouse and stair-tower footprint ways. Primary labeled plan and actually inspected southern panorama, northwest aerial and inner-gate photograph resolve +X towards east-southeast gate and +Z towards the southern Marienbruecke view. Retain signed precinct anchor and heading .381105898007; native +X bearing111.84 degrees, +Z201.84 degrees, -Z21.84 degrees. Correct individually the main and narrower cranked western Palas, stair tower centers, Bower, narrow Knights House cross range, Square Tower and connecting range, and gatehouse shifted from x71 to x58.7 with z3.4 center. The precinct is not extruded or used to stretch the ensemble. Automatic placement remains inactive: the public elevation raster differs by about17m between Palas and gate while the current source court levels differ by1.7m. Coarse elevation includes uncertain roof/canopy and cliff effects, so it cannot justify inventing a vertical reconstruction. A primary section or equivalent reliable relative site survey is still needed.
